summary: Round 7, test review, measured in my own tree at staged hash 87bc946fb5f9. BOTH round-6 minors are genuinely fixed, and I verified the fixes by mutation rather than by reading. (1) 17 is STABLE: five consecutive `--rerun-tasks` runs of both suites are green, so the two new absolute counts are not a flake risk. (2) The named mutant `epoch != ownEpoch && crossFromCheckpoint(...)` now DIES on exactly the two assertions that were relative -- measured 16 against the asserted 17 in both `takeoverCostIsCONSTANTInTheNumberOfPriorTerms` and `...InTheLengthOfTheAncestorsChain`, plus three more kills elsewhere; under the old relative form both sides read 16 and both comparisons passed, so the conversion did real work. (3) ALL FOUR mirror mutants I measured against the 26L assertion die against the two new 17L ones as well, not only elsewhere: `checkpoint.sequence() - 1` gives 27/18/18, `checkpoint.sequence() + 1` gives 25/16/16, `keyFor(hop.from())` gives 25/16/16, and an early `return` that skips the tail gives 24/15/15. Exactness is buying kills at every one of those sites. (4) The deleted comment clauses cost a reader nothing load-bearing: the correctness suite still says WHY it exists separately (`the cost suite is satisfied by a recovery that reads nothing and is wrong`) and now says it without counting the sibling's assertions, and the surviving sentence in LocalSequencerBoundedRecoveryTest -- the `-1` off-by-one measuring 27 -- I re-measured and it is true. (5) Rules 4-5 across the delta: nothing weakened. Two assertions were added and two were changed from relative to absolute, which is strengthening in both cases; no test was deleted; the LocalSequencerFailoverTest threshold move (28->30, 56->58, 20->22, 47->52) is unchanged since the round that already adjudicated it and is carried by ADR-0035. Also measured and NOT filed as findings: `offsets.merge(key, at.nextOffset(), Math::max)` -> `offsets.put(...)` survives both suites, but it is an EQUIVALENT mutant -- `applyChain` never runs before a `crossFromCheckpoint` call, so `offsets` is provably empty at that line and merge and put cannot differ; and the LocalSequencerFailoverTest numbers were re-verified honest in an earlier round. What blocks is new and is not in this round's delta: the I3 barrier on the BOUNDED crossing is unconstrained by any test in the repository, and I have the reproducer.

findings.title: The bounded crossing's I3 barrier is executed by every test and constrained by none: `upTo` on the checkpoint hop can be widened to Long.MAX_VALUE and `./gradlew test` is BUILD SUCCESSFUL
findings.surviving_mutation: In `crossFromCheckpoint`, replace `hops.add(new Hop(chainEpoch, checkpoint.sequence(), upTo));` with `hops.add(new Hop(chainEpoch, checkpoint.sequence(), Long.MAX_VALUE));`. MEASURED IN MY OWN TREE: `./gradlew test` BUILD SUCCESSFUL across every module, and `./gradlew :sequencer:test --rerun-tasks` reports zero failures.
findings.why_the_existing_tests_miss_it: `aCheckpointCoveringEntriesPASTTheBarrierIsNotUsed` pins the CHECKPOINT-level guard (`checkpoint.sequence() - 1 > upTo`) and its fixture has no entries past the barrier at all, so the tail bound is never exercised against one. `theDELTASAfterTheCheckpointAreReplayed` pins where the tail STARTS (measured: both `from` off-by-ones die there) and never where it ENDS -- its chain has no zombie. The mirror guard on the PRE-EXISTING unbounded path IS pinned: widening the other two `new Hop(chainEpoch, 0, limit)` sites the same way fails `CommitLogCrossEpochTest.theCrossingStopsAtTheSlotTheCONTINUENamesRatherThanReadingTheWholePredecessor` with `expected: 6L but was: 105L`. That asymmetry is the finding: the commit added a second construction of the same barrier and no second test.
findings.not_an_equivalent_mutant: Proven by reproducer, not argued. I wrote a 30-line T1 test in my own tree -- epoch 1 holding Continue(0,0,0), delta(1, 6 records), a ZOMBIE delta at slot 2 with 99 records, a LATEST pointer at Checkpoint(sequence 1) which is at or before the barrier and therefore ACCEPTED, and epoch 2 holding Continue(0, 1, 1) -- and recovered epoch 2. Against the staged tree it PASSES at nextOffset = 6. Against the mutant it FAILS at 105. It is the exact fixture shape `CommitLogCrossEpochTest` already uses for the unbounded path, plus one pointer PUT.
findings.remedy: One test in BoundedRecoveryCorrectnessTest, the sibling of `aCheckpointCoveringEntriesPASTTheBarrierIsNotUsed`: an ACCEPTED checkpoint plus entries past the barrier. Nothing in production changes. Note that this is a missing test rather than a live defect -- the shipped code is correct under it -- so the fix adds a test and no prose.
findings.failure_scenario: A leader is fenced and does not stop at once. Its successor lists the chain, sees the end at slot N-1 and writes a CONTINUE naming prevSeq = N-1; the fenced leader then wins the race for slot N and writes a delta there. Everything at or past slot N is a DISCARDED SUFFIX. `hop.upTo()` is the only thing that keeps it out of the history -- `applyChain` returns at `entry.sequence() > hop.upTo()` -- and on the bounded path nothing tests that it is passed correctly. Folding the suffix in re-counts records that were never acknowledged and moves every downstream stream offset, which is I3, silently, and specifically on the path M5's 300 plugin nodes will run.
